Happy writing.

data.value: Use Syncthing, iCloud Drive or Google Drive to carry this vault between computers. Enki reads the local folder; the sync app transfers its files.

data.name: Settings_PrivateSync_Prepare_Body
data.value: 1. Note the vault path above and make a backup outside the folder being synced. 2. Close Enki before moving an existing vault. Sync the entire root folder, including hidden .enki, .sessions, .tasks and .trash folders. 3. Use one sync provider per vault. On another computer, wait for the first download to finish, then choose “Open existing vault” in Enki.

data.name: Settings_PrivateSync_Syncthing_Body
data.value: Add the two devices to each other. Share the exact vault folder from the computer holding the complete copy; on the other, accept it into an empty local folder. Use “Send & Receive” to edit on both. Wait until both devices show “Up to Date” before opening the vault.

data.value: With Enki closed, copy the entire vault into iCloud Drive. Wait for upload and download to finish. Keep the vault folder downloaded on each computer: “Keep Downloaded” in macOS Finder or “Always keep on this device” in Windows Explorer. Then open that local folder in Enki.

data.name: Settings_PrivateSync_Drive_Body
data.value: With Enki closed, place the entire vault in My Drive. Prefer “Mirror files” for a full local copy. With “Stream files”, mark the vault folder “Available offline” on both computers. Wait for all transfers to finish, then open the local folder in Enki.

data.name: Settings_PrivateSync_Daily_Body
data.value: Let Enki finish saving, close it and wait for upload. On the next computer, wait for download before opening Enki. Verify a test note and attachment on both computers. Keep a separate backup: syncing also copies deletions.

data.name: Settings_PrivateSync_Conflicts_Body
data.value: Enki warns about external changes to open notes and lets you compare versions before choosing one. Keep any Syncthing *.sync-conflict-* file until you compare and merge it manually. Tasks and vault settings in JSON are not merged across devices, so avoid editing them on two computers at once.
